The electron in the nth orbit of $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$ is excited to ( $\mathrm{n}+1$ ) orbit using the radiation of energy $1.47 \times 10^{-17} \mathrm{~J}$ (as shown in the diagram). The value of n is $\_\_\_\_$ Given: $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=2.18 \times 10^{-18} \mathrm{~J}$

options.A: For zero order $\mathrm{t}_{1 / 2}=\frac{[\mathrm{A}]_{0}}{2 \mathrm{~K}}$ as concentration decreases half life decreases (Correct statement)
options.B: If order w.r.t. that reactant is zero then it will not affect rate of reaction. (Correct statement)
options.C: Order can be fractional but molecularity can not be (Incorrect statement)
options.D:
For zero order reaction unit is $\mathrm{mol} \mathrm{L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ and for second order reaction unit is $\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \mathrm{Ls}^{-1}$ (Correct statement) n + 1

n
The electron in the nth orbit of $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$ is excited to ( $\mathrm{n}+1$ ) orbit using the radiation of energy $1.47 \times 10^{-17} \mathrm{~J}$ (as shown in the diagram). The value of n is $\_\_\_\_$ Given: $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=2.18 \times 10^{-18} \mathrm{~J}$
Sol. 1
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Delta E=R_{H} Z^{2}\left(\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right) \\
1.47 \times 10^{-17}=2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times 9\left(\frac{1}{n^{2}}-\frac{1}{(n+1)^{2}}\right) \\
\frac{1.47}{1.96}=\frac{3}{4}=\frac{1}{n^{2}}-\frac{1}{(n+1)^{2}}
\end{array}$$

So, $\mathrm{n}=1$

88. For a metal ion, the calculated magnetic moment is 4.90BM. This metal ion has $\_\_\_\_$ number of unpaired electrons.
Sol. 4
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mu=4.90 \mathrm{BM} . \\
\mu=\sqrt{\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{n}+2)}
\end{array}$$

So, $\mathrm{n}=4$
